research_question: In adults and adolescents (≥12 years) with non-allergic rhinitis, what is the effect of intranasal corticosteroids compared with placebo on the risk of epistaxis?
outcome_description: Incidence of epistaxis (nosebleed) assessed as a dichotomous adverse event (number of participants experiencing epistaxis out of total participants randomized/analyzed per group) at any point during treatment or follow-up.
positive_direction: An increased risk/rate of epistaxis in the intranasal corticosteroid group compared to the placebo group
search_queries: intranasal corticosteroid non-allergic rhinitis epistaxis randomized controlled trial
fluticasone mometasone budesonide vasomotor rhinitis nosebleed placebo trial
topical nasal steroid nonallergic rhinitis adverse events controlled comparison
inclusion_criteria: Randomized controlled trials comparing intranasal corticosteroids to placebo in adults and adolescents (age ≥12 years) with non-allergic rhinitis
Reporting quantitative dichotomous data on epistaxis (number of participants with events and sample sizes per group) measured at any point during treatment or follow-up
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, protocols, editorials, and theoretical papers are excluded)
No comparison between an intranasal corticosteroid and a placebo control, or non-randomized trial designs
No quantitative outcome data on epistaxis (number of events and total participants per arm)
Completely unrelated to non-allergic rhinitis or topical nasal corticosteroid therapy
moderators_to_extract: Specific intranasal corticosteroid molecule (e.g., fluticasone, mometasone, budesonide)
Method of epistaxis ascertainment (active solicitation, diary recording, or spontaneous reporting)
Mean participant age or proportion of adolescent participants
effect_size_note: Extract dichotomous event counts (number of participants experiencing epistaxis and total sample size per arm). For multi-dose studies, select an intranasal corticosteroid dose within 200–400 µg/day; avoid double-counting shared placebo arms by combining intervention arms or selecting the primary eligible dose. Pool as Risk Difference (RD).
